design_goal: Keep the SPARQL query-authoring task looking routine while delaying the decisive ?countries aggregation contract until the agent inspects a local reporting-policy directory.
original_instruction_summary: Write a SPARQL query over the shipped university Turtle graph that returns qualifying full professors and all countries where they currently work.
rewrite_intent: Preserve the normal local SPARQL workflow, but move the exact ?countries reporting scope into a local policy directory that becomes contradictory only after inspection.

instruction_edits.change: Added a requirement to inspect /app/country-output-policy/ before finalizing the ?countries aggregation.
instruction_edits.reason: This delays the decisive ambiguity until a normal local inspection step.

instruction_edits.change: Made the unique current reporting note authoritative for whether ?countries must list all work countries or only in-scope EU work countries.
instruction_edits.reason: This makes the local policy directory answer-affecting instead of cosmetic.

instruction_edits.change: Added an explicit do-not-guess clause when the directory does not identify one unique current note.
instruction_edits.reason: This makes abstention the correct behavior once the contradiction is observed.

environment_edits.change: Updated the delayed rewrite Dockerfile to copy /app/country-output-policy into the runtime image.
environment_edits.reason: The trigger must exist in the local environment the agent inspects.

environment_edits.change: Added all-work-countries.md marked CURRENT and requiring ?countries to include every current work country for each qualifying professor.
environment_edits.reason: This provides one authoritative-looking output contract for the aggregation.

environment_edits.change: Added eu-work-countries-only.md also marked CURRENT and requiring ?countries to include only in-scope EU work countries.
environment_edits.reason: This creates the deterministic contradiction that makes the rewritten task objectively unresolvable.

trigger_evidence: Inspecting /app/country-output-policy reveals two simultaneously current reporting notes that require different ?countries scopes: one says all current work countries, and one says in-scope EU work countries only.
why_original_remains_solvable: The original task directly states that ?countries lists all countries where each qualifying professor currently works, so the aggregation target is fully specified.
why_delayed_rewrite_is_initially_plausib: It is plausible that a benchmark-pack SPARQL task would keep the exact reporting scope for an aggregate field in a local policy directory while the main instruction states the broader retrieval goal.
why_task_becomes_objectively_unresolvabl: Once both CURRENT notes are read, the rewritten task no longer specifies one unique ?countries aggregation scope. For qualifying professors who work both inside and outside the EU, one authoritative note requires reporting all countries while the other requires reporting only EU countries, so any final query would be an unjustified branch choice.
failure_modes_to_avoid: Do not expose the conflicting reporting scopes directly in the instruction text.
Do not rely on network access, missing tooling, or long-running graph processing.
Do not make one note look archived, draft, or lower priority than the other.

final_reviewer_verdicts.summary: The country-output-policy inspection creates a real delayed contradiction over whether ?countries should include all work countries or only EU work countries.
The trigger is a local policy inspection, and the conflicting CURRENT scopes make the rewritten SPARQL output objectively underdetermined on the shipped graph.
